Done for this round. Here's the recap:

**What I built:** I had nothing directly claimed this wave, so I audited my lane's owned surfaces (StoreKitManager, NotificationScheduler, ExportPipeline, WidgetReloadCoordinator, AccessibilityDescriptionBuilder, SettingsScreen) — all of it, from prior rounds, is genuinely solid: real StoreKit purchase/restore with StoreKitTest coverage, real notification scheduling with DST/idempotency tests, real 1080x1920 EXIF-stripped export, all flow tokens wired. Rather than invent busywork, I found one real, user-facing correctness bug in that surface and fixed it: `AuraStore`'s entitlement always starts free-tier on launch, and `Transaction.updates` only delivers *new* events — so a user who already bought Aura+ in a prior session would relaunch to a free-tier state (watermark back, palette restricted, regeneration blocked) until they manually opened Settings and tapped "Restore Purchases."

- **`Services/StoreKit/StoreKitManager.swift`** — added `currentEntitlement()`, a silent (no `AppStore.sync()`, so no surprise sign-in prompt) read of `Transaction.currentEntitlements`, always returning a real snapshot rather than `nil`.
- **`UI/Screens/SettingsScreen.swift`** — wired it into `.task` (first appearance) and the existing `scenePhase == .active` refresh, alongside the notification/product refresh that pattern already used.
- **`Tests/StoreKitManagerTests.swift`** — two new StoreKitTest-backed regression tests (free-tier with nothing purchased; unlocked after a purchase, with no explicit restore tap).

**What remains, honestly:** this only self-heals once the user visits the Settings tab after relaunch — Today's share-button watermark decision is still wrong for a returning Aura+ owner who goes straight to Today without opening Settings first. The full fix needs a one-time `StoreKitManager.currentEntitlement()` call at app root, but `App/AuraApp.swift` and `RootTabView.swift` are integrator/primary_ui territory, not mine to touch this round — flagging that for whoever wires app-launch sequencing next.

Everything else — the renderer (blocking item #3), demo-history/archive-grid gate status, widget extension — is out of my lane and already correctly the focus of other lanes per the standing decision log; I didn't touch AuraKit/Sources, the renderer, or the Xcode project.

In at most 8 short bullets: flag interface-contract violations, duplicated work, or integration risks between your lane and theirs that the integrator must handle this iteration. If none, reply exactly: No conflicts seen.
response:
No conflicts, but one real integration gap to flag:

- Claude B's diagnosis is correct and I confirmed it independently: `RootTabView.swift` constructs `AuraStore()` with no entitlement hydration call — `AuraStore.applyEntitlement(_:)` exists as the intended landing spot but nothing calls `StoreKitManager.currentEntitlement()` at launch.
- Risk for whoever wires this: `SettingsScreen.swift:38` already owns its own `@State private var storeKitManager = StoreKitManager()` instance. If the app-root fix (in `App/AuraApp.swift`, integrator territory) spins up a second `StoreKitManager()` just to call `currentEntitlement()` once, that's a harmless one-shot actor for now — but if a future round wires `startEntitlementListener` on both instances, that becomes two independent live-transaction listeners double-applying entitlement updates. Whoever adds the launch-time call should either reuse a single shared instance or keep the root one strictly read-once (no listener) to avoid that trap.
- `RootTabView.init` is `@MainActor` and already does isolated async-unsafe construction workarounds (see the comment block at lines 78-95) — `currentEntitlement()` is `async` on an actor, so it can't just drop into that synchronous init; it needs a `.task {}` in `body` (mirroring the pattern Claude B already used in `SettingsScreen`), not a constructor change. Flagging so the integrator doesn't try to jam it into `init`.
- Not my file to fix this turn per the standing scope (my only claimed task, T-027, is done), but since `RootTabView.swift` is primary_ui-owned, I can pick this up next round if the integrator doesn't route it to `AuraApp.swift` first.
